articles.summary:
More than 100,000 people marched in Paris on Saturday over school funding and soaring living costs, challenging President Emmanuel Macron's government as police fired tear gas and water cannons near the end of the protest.
Paris police estimated turnout at 110,000, with demonstrators mobilizing despite restrictions that confined the march to the city's southeastern edge, away from the center.
Police used tear gas in several cities, including Lyon, Clermont-Ferrand, and Strasbourg, and water cannons in Nice and Nantes, French media reported. In Marseille, officers fired tear gas during clashes with several dozen people near the march's endpoint.
The Paris prosecutor's office said 64 people had been arrested in connection with Saturday's demonstration and 40 placed in police custody. Those arrested included six minors. articles.title: UK tells Britons to stockpile essentials
articles.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has urged Britons to be better prepared for emergencies saying that unexpected events are becoming increasingly common. The remarks came as the government rolled out its new ‘Be Ready’ initiative, which asks households to keep essential supplies at home for three days.“We're having the conversation with people about being better prepared because we're living in a world where unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common,” Burnham said on Friday.Also Read: Immigration to UK from third-world countries, including Pakistan, will end entirely, British MP Rupert Lowe warnsWhy is the UK asking people to prepare for emergencies?The advisory comes amid concerns about disruptions caused by severe weather, cyberattacks and other unexpected events.The UK has experienced storms, droughts, extreme heat and wildfires in recent years. These events can damage infrastructure and disrupt essential services. They can also affect access to electricity, water, phone networks and the internet.Also Read: Don't panic: UK govt tells Britons to 'be ready' for emergenciesCybersecurity incidents have added to these concerns. Recent cyberattacks affecting French supermarket chains disrupted refrigeration systems. Stores were forced to discard spoiled food. Separately, a software security incident involving PHP, a programming language used by many websites, prompted organisations to shut down websites.The campaign also reflects a wider European push for emergency preparedness. France, Ireland and the Netherlands have issued similar guidance. These recommendations encourage households to prepare to manage disruptions for three days.What does the emergency checklist include?The official ‘Be Ready’ checklist recommends keeping enough essential supplies at home to manage for three days. It covers eight broad categories.Water- Bottled water for three days.- At least three litres per person per day for drinking.- Additional water for cooking and washing.2. Food- Three days' worth of non-perishable food.- Long-lasting food that does not need refrigeration or cooking.- Examples include tinned meat, fish and vegetables, dried fruit and nuts.- The government recommends choosing food that household members would normally eat.3. Hygiene- Hand sanitiser.- Wet wipes.- Essential hygiene and bathroom products.4. Light and warmth- A torch and spare batteries.- Blankets and sleeping bags.- Warm clothing to help households cope if heating is disrupted.5. Communication and information- A battery-powered or wind-up FM radio to receive updates during outages.- A charged power bank to keep phones running.6. Money and documents- Cash in a mix of coins and banknotes.- Payment cards in case electronic payment systems or ATMs stop working.- Copies of important documents, including identification.- A written list of important phone numbers.- Information about regular medication and dosages.7. Medical and health supplies- A first-aid kit with basic supplies.- Essential medicines and other medical supplies.8. Baby and pet supplies- Baby formula, nappies and wipes for households with infants.- Ready-to-feed formula is recommended. Preparing powdered formula safely may be difficult if water cannot be boiled.- Pet food and bottled water for animals.The government has advised people not to buy everything at once. Households should first check what they already have. They can then identify missing items and add them during regular shopping trips. This approach also helps spread the cost.The checklist recommends reviewing supplies every six months. People should check expiry dates and replace items when necessary. They should also update their kits as household needs change.The government also encouraged people to speak to their neighbours. They can exchange contact details and discuss how to help one another during an outage. Those with extra supplies may consider donating them to people who cannot afford to prepare their own households.The government has separately encouraged eligible households to sign up to the Priority Services Register. The register helps electricity, gas and water providers identify customers who may need additional assistance during service interruptions.

articles.summary: United Nations: The head of the UN nuclear agency said on Friday that he expects the use of nuclear power could more than triple by 2060.Rafael Grossi said in the International Atomic Energy Agency's annual report to the UN General Assembly that this will be driven by electrification, data centres powered by artificial intelligence and "technology companies' appetite for reliable, carbon-free power".Also read: Zelenskiy says Ukrainian, Russian and US negotiators to meet in early November in Abu DhabiNuclear energy is seen by a growing number of countries as key to improving their energy security, he said, stressing that it is on par with solar energy and "safer than every other option"."In 2025, more than 400 operating reactors in more than 30 countries produced 10 per cent of global electricity and a quarter of its low-carbon electricity," the IAEA director-general said. "More than 60 new reactors are under construction and the projections for future nuclear capacity have shifted dramatically upward."In addition to the growing use of nuclear energy for peaceful purposes, Grossi spoke about the nuclear programmes in Iran and North Korea, the "unprecedented threats to nuclear safety" from the war in Ukraine, and worrying reports that other countries he did not name are talking about acquiring nuclear weapons.On Iran, whose nuclear sites were struck by the US last year before the US and Israel launched a war on February 28, Grossi told UN member nations that the necessary technical work for a diplomatic agreement has been done."I call on the parties to redouble their efforts towards agreeing a diplomatic solution that includes the IAEA's indispensable verification role, without which no agreement can be sustainable," he said. "IAEA inspectors must be able to return to Iran expeditiously. That requires a return to the negotiating table."In North Korea, where leader Kim Jong Un has a growing nuclear programme without any IAEA oversight, Grossi warned that it "stands as a stark reminder of the consequences when red lines are crossed" in violation of UN Security Council resolutions banning nuclear weapons production.Also read: Melania Trump brokers Russia-Ukraine ceasefire in war-hit Oleshky, White House saysIn Ukraine, he singled out the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, Europe's largest, saying it remains "in a precarious position" with frequent power losses, limited back-up diesel supplies "and military activity threatening the plant and the people who work there".On a positive note, Grossi said the IAEA has made "significant progress" in clarifying and resolving outstanding questions regarding Syria's nuclear activities after nearly two decades of uncertainty. That is as a result of engaging with the government of interim President Ahmad al-Sharaa, he said.He reported in September that the Bashar Assad-era government -- which was ousted in December 2024 by opposition forces led by al-Sharaa -- was constructing a nuclear reactor that was configured to produce fissile material for possible use in nuclear weapons.

articles.title: India business sentiment rebounds in Q2 FY27: NCAER
articles.summary: India’s business sentiment rebounded in the second quarter of this fiscal year, with the Business Confidence Index (BCI) rising to 107.8 from 99.8 in the April–June quarter, ending a four-quarter period of moderation driven by ongoing geopolitical tensions, according to the latest NCAER Business Expectations Survey.Conducted in September by the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER), the survey sampled 502 companies across different sizes in six major cities: Delhi NCR in the north, Bengaluru and Chennai in the south, Kolkata in the east, and Mumbai and Pune in the west."Though BCI improved, it was lower than the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year (142.6 in 2025−26: Q2)," it said.Also read: India October business growth hits 4-month high; hiring stalls, PMI showsThe BCI evaluates four key parameters: expectations of improved macro-economic conditions over the next six months, expectations of better firm financial health over the next six months, a favorable current investment climate, and present capacity utilization at or near optimal levels.All four parameters recorded gains, driving the quarter-over-quarter uptick in business sentiment."The share of firms expecting 'overall economic conditions to improve in the next six months' increased from 43 per cent in 2026-27: Q1 to 50 per cent in 2026-27: Q2," NCAER said.Confidence regarding firm financial prospects over the coming six months expanded from 37% in Q1 to 41% in Q2. Similarly, positive assessments of the current investment climate grew from 26% to 30%. Opinions on optimal capacity utilization also saw an increase, climbing from 91% in the first quarter to 94% in the second.Segment-wise, the BCI for MSMEs moved up from 93 to 100, while for large enterprises it rose from 111.6 to 120.3.NCAER's Bornali Bhandari, who led the survey, said, "The data indicate a broad-based recovery in sentiments across both MSMEs and large firms"."Overall business prospects improved both domestically and externally, and cost sentiments have moderated," she added.
